title: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after customer accounts compromised
date_note: TfL says it became aware on 16 November 2026; The Register published on 19 November 2026.
summary: The Register reports Transport for London took its Oyster photocard website offline after customers received emails asking them to create accounts they already had, which TfL traced to a compromise. TfL says around 265,000 customers were potentially affected, has told the Information Commissioner's Office, and says passwords, payment card details and journey data were not compromised. No attacker has been named.
plain: TfL shut down the website used for Oyster photocards after attackers got into customer accounts. Existing photocards still work at barriers; TfL will ask customers to change their passwords.
exec: A breach at a major transport operator exposes personal data of around 265,000 customers, including children and students, and brings regulator notification.
action: If you hold an Oyster photocard, change your password and security questions when asked, change it anywhere you reused it, and treat unexpected account emails with care.
impact: Photocard website offline; renewals and journey history only via customer services; around 265,000 customers potentially affected.

validation.note: The Register quotes TfL's director Shashi Verma. The BBC reports the same breach but its page could not be read here, so it is not counted.
